The formula for the derivative of [MATH: \textrm{arccot}] is

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\textrm {arccot } x) = -\dfrac 1 {1+x^2}.]

sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: f(x) =3 x\, \textrm {arccsc }x,] calculate [MATH: f'(x).]

The formula for the derivative of [MATH: \textrm{arccsc}] is

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\textrm {arccsc } x) = -\dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}} \, .]

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

[MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (d)/(dx)(3xarccscx); = 3(d)/(dx)(xarccscx); = 3(x ⋅ (d)/(dx)(arccscx) + arccscx ⋅ (d)/(dx)(x)); = 3x(− (1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1))) + 3arccscx ⋅ 1; = − (3x)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)) + 3arccscx.]

sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{\textrm{arcsec } x}{\textrm{arccsc } x},] calculate [MATH: f'(x).]
sections.readable_text: If [MATH: f(x) = \dfrac{\textrm{arcsec } x}{\textrm{arccsc } x},] calculate [MATH: f'(x).]

sections.normalized_html:
Here, we let [MATH: u(x) = \textrm{arcsec } x] and [MATH: v(x) = \textrm{arccsc } x], and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae [MATH: u'(x) = \dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}} \quad \text{and} \quad v'(x) = -\dfrac 1 {|x| \sqrt {x^2 - 1}}.]

Therefore, [MATH: f^{′}(x)|= (u^{′}(x) ⋅ v(x) − u(x) ⋅ v^{′}(x))/([v(x)]^{2}); = ((1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)) ⋅ arccscx − arcsecx ⋅ (− (1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1))))/(arccsc^{2}x); = ((1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)))(arccscx + arcsecx)/(arccsc^{2}x); = (arccscx + arcsecx)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)arccsc^{2}x).]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can calculate the derivatives of the inverse reciprocal trigonometric functions by using their definition and the chain rule, similar to how we did for the inverse trigonometric functions. When we do so, we get the following results:

Content:
[MATH: (d)/(dx)(arcsecx)|= (1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)); (d)/(dx)(arccscx)|= − (1)/(|x|sqrt(x^{2} − 1)); (d)/(dx)(arccotx)|= − (1)/(1 + x^{2})]

---

Item 2 — Example: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions

Example Prompt:
Calculate [MATH: \dfrac {\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}] if [MATH: y = 2 \,\textrm {arccot } x.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The formula for the derivative of [MATH: \textrm{arccot}] is

[MATH: \dfrac{\textrm d}{\textrm d x}(\textrm {arccot } x) = -\dfrac 1 {1+x^2}.]

Using the formula above, we obtain

[MATH: (dy)/(dx)|= (d)/(dx)(2arccotx); = 2 ⋅ (d)/(dx)(arccotx); = 2 ⋅ (− (1)/(1 + x^{2})); = − (2)/(1 + x^{2}).]
